/-!
# Danzer sets

A *Danzer set* in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of points that meets every convex body of volume $1$.
Danzer asked whether such a set can have bounded density, i.e. growth rate $O(r^d)$.
Conway's *dead fly problem* (also due to Boshernitzan) asks whether such a set can be
uniformly discrete, i.e. whether distinct points of the set can be kept at least some fixed
positive distance apart. Both problems are open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Danzer set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danzer_set)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ad22] Adiceam, F., _Around the Danzer problem and the construction of dense forests_.
  L'Enseignement Mathématique 68 (2022). [arXiv:2010.06756](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06756)
- [SoWe16] Solomon, Y. and Weiss, B., _Dense forests and Danzer sets_.
  Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 49 (2016). [arXiv:1406.3807](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.3807)
- [SSW17] Solan, O., Solomon, Y. and Weiss, B., _On problems of Danzer and Gowers and dynamics
  on the space of closed subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$_. IMRN (2017).
  [arXiv:1510.07179](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07179)
-/

def IsDanzerSet {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=

blocks.docstring:
A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` is a *Danzer set* if it intersects every convex body (compact convex
nonempty set) of volume `1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `ConvexBody` and `MeasureTheory.volume` are used as the building blocks; no existing predicate combines them.
justification.name: DanzerSet.IsDanzerSet
justification.why_needed: No notion of a set meeting every unit-volume convex body exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: IsDanzerSet
blocks.text:
/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` is a *Danzer set* if it intersects every convex body (compact convex
nonempty set) of volume `1`. -/
def IsDanzerSet {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ K : ConvexBody (ℝ^d), volume (K : Set (ℝ^d)) = 1 → (S ∩ K).Nonempty

blocks.docstring:
A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` has *bounded density*, i.e. growth rate `O(r ^ d)`: there is a constant `C`
such that, for every `r ≥ 1`, the closed ball of radius `r` about the origin contains only
finitely many points of `S`, and at most `C * r ^ d` of them. Equivalently,
$\limsup_{r \to \infty} \#(S \cap B(0, r)) / r^d < \infty$.

The finiteness condition is needed because `Set.ncard` of an infinite set is `0`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.upperDensity (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Set/Density.lean), Asymptotics.IsBigO, Filter.limsup in ℝ≥0∞ with Set.encard.
justification.name: DanzerSet.HasBoundedDensity
justification.why_needed: Need 'growth rate O(r^d)' / finite upper density for point sets in ℝ^d. `Set.upperDensity` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib is only for ordered types with `LocallyFiniteOrderBot` (ℕ-like), not for subsets of Euclidean space; `Asymptotics.IsBigO` would still need a separate local-finiteness clause because `ncard` of an infinite set is 0.

blocks.name: HasBoundedDensity
blocks.text:
/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` has *bounded density*, i.e. growth rate `O(r ^ d)`: there is a constant `C`
such that, for every `r ≥ 1`, the closed ball of radius `r` about the origin contains only
finitely many points of `S`, and at most `C * r ^ d` of them. Equivalently,
$\limsup_{r \to \infty} \#(S \cap B(0, r)) / r^d < \infty$.

The finiteness condition is needed because `Set.ncard` of an infinite set is `0`. -/
def HasBoundedDensity {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ r : ℝ, 1 ≤ r →
    (S ∩ closedBall 0 r).Finite ∧ (S ∩ closedBall 0 r).ncard ≤ C * r ^ d

def IsUniformlyDiscrete {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ S.Pairwise (fun x y => r ≤ dist x y)
blocks.docstring:
A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` is *uniformly discrete* if there is `r > 0` such that any two distinct
points of `S` are at distance at least `r`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Metric.IsSeparated (Mathlib, strict edist bound) and Metric.IsSeparated' (FormalConjecturesForMathlib, non-strict edist bound); `∃ ε > 0, IsSeparated ε S` is equivalent but less transparent (ε : ℝ≥0∞, edist).
justification.name: DanzerSet.IsUniformlyDiscrete
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no `UniformlyDiscrete`/`Delone` predicate; the direct statement (∃ r > 0, pairwise dist ≥ r) is the definition used by all three sources.

blocks.name: IsUniformlyDiscrete
blocks.text:
/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` is *uniformly discrete* if there is `r > 0` such that any two distinct
points of `S` are at distance at least `r`. -/
def IsUniformlyDiscrete {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ S.Pairwise (fun x y => r ≤ dist x y)

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem not_isDanzerSet_empty (d : ℕ) : ¬ IsDanzerSet (∅ : Set (ℝ^d)) := by
  intro h
  let e := PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ fun _ : Fin d => ℝ
  refine (h ⟨e ⁻¹' Set.Icc 0 1, (convex_Icc _ _).linear_preimage (e : ℝ^d →ₗ[ℝ] Fin d → ℝ),
    e.toHomeomorph.isCompact_preimage.mpr isCompact_Icc, ⟨0, by simp⟩⟩ ?_).ne_empty (by simp)
  rw [ConvexBody.coe_mk, PiLp.coe_continuousLinearEquiv,
    (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin d)).measure_preimage measurableSet_Icc.nullMeasurableSet,
    Real.volume_Icc_pi]
  simp

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem not_hasBoundedDensity_univ {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) :
    ¬ HasBoundedDensity (Set.univ : Set (ℝ^d)) := by
  haveI : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
  rintro ⟨C, hC⟩
  have h1 := (hC 1 le_rfl).1.measure_zero (volume : Measure (ℝ^d))
  have h2 := measure_closedBall_pos (volume : Measure (ℝ^d)) (0 : ℝ^d) one_pos
  simp at h1
  exact h2.ne' h1

infinitely many of its points.

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem HasBoundedDensity.of_finite {d : ℕ} {S : Set (ℝ^d)} (hS : S.Finite) :
    HasBoundedDensity S := by
  refine ⟨S.ncard, fun r hr => ⟨hS.subset Set.inter_subset_left, ?_⟩⟩
  calc ((S ∩ closedBall 0 r).ncard : ℝ) ≤ S.ncard := by
        exact_mod_cast Set.ncard_le_ncard Set.inter_subset_left hS
    _ = S.ncard * 1 := (mul_one _).symm
    _ ≤ S.ncard * r ^ d := by gcongr; exact one_le_pow₀ hr
blocks.docstring: A finite set has bounded density.

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem danzer_set.parts.i (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    (answer(sorry) : ℕ → Prop) d ↔
      ∃ S : Set (ℝ^d), IsDanzerSet S ∧ HasBoundedDensity S := by

blocks.docstring:
**Danzer's problem.** Let $d \ge 2$. Does there exist a Danzer set in $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e. a
set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ meeting every convex body of volume $1$, of bounded density,
i.e. with $\#(S \cap B(0, r)) = O(r^d)$?

The answer is unknown and may in principle depend on the dimension $d$, so it is recorded as a
predicate on $d$. The case $d = 1$ is excluded because it is trivial (the integers form a Danzer
set of bounded density in $\mathbb{R}$). By scaling, requiring volume exactly $1$ is no
restriction: the problem is the same for any fixed positive volume.

blocks.docstring:
**Conway's dead fly problem** (also due to Boshernitzan). Let $d \ge 2$. Does there exist a
uniformly discrete Danzer set in $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e. a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ meeting
every convex body of volume $1$ such that, for some $r > 0$, any two distinct points of $S$ are
at distance at least $r$?

Conway asked this for the plane $d = 2$; Boshernitzan independently asked it in general
dimension. Such a set is automatically a Delone set of growth rate $O(r^d)$, so a positive answer
would also give a positive answer to Danzer's problem in the same dimension. The answer may in
principle depend on the dimension $d$, so it is recorded as a predicate on $d$.

claims.decomposer_note: Danzer's problem (the 'bounded density' half): for dimension d ≥ 2 (d = 1 is trivial, ℤ works), does there exist a set S ⊆ ℝ^d meeting every convex body of volume 1 with finite upper density limsup_{r→∞} |S ∩ B(0,r)| / r^d < ∞ (equivalently growth O(r^d); the unit-volume normalization and the restriction to boxes/ellipsoids are equivalent by scaling and John's theorem); the answer is unknown and could in principle depend on d, so quantifier placement over d relative to answer(sorry) needs care.
claims.reviewer_why: c06's declaration used verbatim (bespoke `IsDanzerSet` = meets every Mathlib `ConvexBody` of Lebesgue `volume` 1, exactly Wikipedia's/Adiceam's 'convex body of volume 1'; `HasBoundedDensity` = ∃ C, ∀ r ≥ 1, S ∩ closedBall 0 r finite with ncard ≤ C r^d, which is exactly growth O(r^d) / limsup |S∩B(0,r)|/r^d < ∞; the Finite guard prevents ncard's 0-on-infinite default from making ℝ^d a 'bounded density' set). Dimension d ≥ 2 is a theorem parameter and the answer is a dimension-indexed predicate `(answer(sorry) : ℕ → Prop) d`, following ErdosProblems/592 and OpenQuantumProblems/13, so the answer may depend on d as the notes require. All eight candidates were mathematically faithful for this slot; c06 was chosen for clarity, proved API tests, and the precedent-matching answer form (c01's `ℕ → Bool` coercion, c02's subtype, c03's linter-disabled `answer(sorry) ↔` with binders, c07's `show ℕ → Prop from` were less idiomatic; c04/c05's ℝ≥0∞-limsup definitions are correct but rely on ENNReal division conventions). Added c08's proved test `not_isDanzerSet_empty` (unit cube has volume 1) and `not_hasBoundedDensity_univ` as normalization/boundary checks.

claims.reviewer_why: c06's declaration used verbatim: for each d ≥ 2, `(answer(sorry) : ℕ → Prop) d ↔ ∃ S, IsDanzerSet S ∧ IsUniformlyDiscrete S`, where `IsUniformlyDiscrete S` = ∃ r > 0, S.Pairwise (r ≤ dist · ·), i.e. distinct points at distance ≥ r — the Boshernitzan–Conway uniformly discrete Danzer set problem (Adiceam, Problem 'Boshernitzan–Conway'), stated in general dimension as the survey does, with Conway's planar original as the case d = 2. Gowers' solved bounded-coverage variant is not stated. All candidates were faithful; c08's `Metric.IsSeparated` (strict, ℝ≥0∞) is equivalent existentially but less transparent.

/-!

A *Danzer set* in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of points that meets every convex body of volume $1$.
Danzer asked whether such a set can have bounded density, i.e. growth rate $O(r^d)$.
Conway's *dead fly problem* (also due to Boshernitzan) asks whether such a set can be

- [Wikipedia, Danzer set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danzer_set)

open MeasureTheory Metric

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace DanzerSet

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` is a *Danzer set* if it intersects every convex body (compact convex
nonempty set) of volume `1`. -/
def IsDanzerSet {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ K : ConvexBody (ℝ^d), volume (K : Set (ℝ^d)) = 1 → (S ∩ K).Nonempty

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` has *bounded density*, i.e. growth rate `O(r ^ d)`: there is a constant `C`
such that, for every `r ≥ 1`, the closed ball of radius `r` about the origin contains only
finitely many points of `S`, and at most `C * r ^ d` of them. Equivalently,
$\limsup_{r \to \infty} \#(S \cap B(0, r)) / r^d < \infty$.

The finiteness condition is needed because `Set.ncard` of an infinite set is `0`. -/
def HasBoundedDensity {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ r : ℝ, 1 ≤ r →
    (S ∩ closedBall 0 r).Finite ∧ (S ∩ closedBall 0 r).ncard ≤ C * r ^ d

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ^d` is *uniformly discrete* if there is `r > 0` such that any two distinct
points of `S` are at distance at least `r`. -/
def IsUniformlyDiscrete {d : ℕ} (S : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ S.Pairwise (fun x y => r ≤ dist x y)

/-- The whole space is a Danzer set. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isDanzerSet_univ (d : ℕ) : IsDanzerSet (Set.univ : Set (ℝ^d)) := fun K _ => by
  simpa using K.nonempty

/-- The empty set is not a Danzer set, since the unit cube $[0,1]^d$ has volume one. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem not_isDanzerSet_empty (d : ℕ) : ¬ IsDanzerSet (∅ : Set (ℝ^d)) := by
  intro h
  let e := PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ fun _ : Fin d => ℝ
  refine (h ⟨e ⁻¹' Set.Icc 0 1, (convex_Icc _ _).linear_preimage (e : ℝ^d →ₗ[ℝ] Fin d → ℝ),
    e.toHomeomorph.isCompact_preimage.mpr isCompact_Icc, ⟨0, by simp⟩⟩ ?_).ne_empty (by simp)
  rw [ConvexBody.coe_mk, PiLp.coe_continuousLinearEquiv,
    (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin d)).measure_preimage measurableSet_Icc.nullMeasurableSet,
    Real.volume_Icc_pi]
  simp

/-- The whole space `ℝ^d` (for `d ≥ 1`) does not have bounded density: the unit ball contains
infinitely many of its points. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem not_hasBoundedDensity_univ {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) :
    ¬ HasBoundedDensity (Set.univ : Set (ℝ^d)) := by
  haveI : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
  rintro ⟨C, hC⟩
  have h1 := (hC 1 le_rfl).1.measure_zero (volume : Measure (ℝ^d))
  have h2 := measure_closedBall_pos (volume : Measure (ℝ^d)) (0 : ℝ^d) one_pos
  simp at h1
  exact h2.ne' h1

/-- A finite set has bounded density. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem HasBoundedDensity.of_finite {d : ℕ} {S : Set (ℝ^d)} (hS : S.Finite) :
    HasBoundedDensity S := by
  refine ⟨S.ncard, fun r hr => ⟨hS.subset Set.inter_subset_left, ?_⟩⟩
  calc ((S ∩ closedBall 0 r).ncard : ℝ) ≤ S.ncard := by

    _ = S.ncard * 1 := (mul_one _).symm
    _ ≤ S.ncard * r ^ d := by gcongr; exact one_le_pow₀ hr

/-- The empty set is uniformly discrete. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isUniformlyDiscrete_empty (d : ℕ) : IsUniformlyDiscrete (∅ : Set (ℝ^d)) :=
  ⟨1, one_pos, Set.pairwise_empty _⟩

/--
**Danzer's problem.** Let $d \ge 2$. Does there exist a Danzer set in $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e. a
set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ meeting every convex body of volume $1$, of bounded density,
i.e. with $\#(S \cap B(0, r)) = O(r^d)$?

The answer is unknown and may in principle depend on the dimension $d$, so it is recorded as a
predicate on $d$. The case $d = 1$ is excluded because it is trivial (the integers form a Danzer
set of bounded density in $\mathbb{R}$). By scaling, requiring volume exactly $1$ is no
restriction: the problem is the same for any fixed positive volume.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem danzer_set.parts.i (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    (answer(sorry) : ℕ → Prop) d ↔
      ∃ S : Set (ℝ^d), IsDanzerSet S ∧ HasBoundedDensity S := by
  sorry

/--
**Conway's dead fly problem** (also due to Boshernitzan). Let $d \ge 2$. Does there exist a
uniformly discrete Danzer set in $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e. a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ meeting
every convex body of volume $1$ such that, for some $r > 0$, any two distinct points of $S$ are
at distance at least $r$?

Conway asked this for the plane $d = 2$; Boshernitzan independently asked it in general
dimension. Such a set is automatically a Delone set of growth rate $O(r^d)$, so a positive answer
would also give a positive answer to Danzer's problem in the same dimension. The answer may in
principle depend on the dimension $d$, so it is recorded as a predicate on $d$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem danzer_set.parts.ii (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    (answer(sorry) : ℕ → Prop) d ↔
      ∃ S : Set (ℝ^d), IsDanzerSet S ∧ IsUniformlyDiscrete S := by
  sorry

end DanzerSet

items: Dimension handling: both slots take (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) as parameters and use a dimension-dependent answer `(answer(sorry) : ℕ → Prop) d` (precedent: ErdosProblems/592, OpenQuantumProblems/13). This follows the sources (Adiceam Problem 1 'in dimension n ≥ 2', Solomon–Weiss 'for d ≥ 2'), and lets the answer vary with d. The alternative `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ d ≥ 2, ∃ S, ...` would conflate dimensions. d = 1 is excluded as in the sources (ℤ is trivially a uniformly discrete Danzer set of bounded density in ℝ). The linter-preferred `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ...` form is not used because the linter's suggestion would force a single answer for all d.

Convex bodies: `ConvexBody (ℝ^d)` (Mathlib: compact, convex, nonempty) with `volume K = 1`, matching the article's 'convex body whose volume is one'. Some papers say 'convex set of volume 1'; the existence problems are equivalent (a convex set of volume 2 contains a compact convex body of volume exactly 1, and dilation by a constant preserves bounded density and uniform discreteness), so this choice does not change either problem. `volume` on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` is the standard Lebesgue measure (unit cube has volume 1).

Bounded density formalized as explicit O(r^d) growth: ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ r ≥ 1, (S ∩ closedBall 0 r).Finite ∧ ncard ≤ C * r^d. The `Finite` conjunct is essential: `Set.ncard` of an infinite set is 0, which would otherwise make the whole space 'bounded density'. Restricting to r ≥ 1 avoids the r → 0 issue when 0 ∈ S. This is equivalent to the Wikipedia article's density definition limsup_{r→∞} |S ∩ B_d(r)| / V_d(r) < ∞ (and to Adiceam's limsup |S ∩ B(0,T)|/T^n < ∞) since they differ by the constant V_d(1) and a finite initial segment.

Uniform discreteness ('bounded separation') formalized directly as ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ S.Pairwise (r ≤ dist · ·), i.e. inf over distinct pairs of ‖x − y‖ is > 0. Non-strict ≥ r matches Solomon–Weiss ('distance ... is at least r'); equivalent to Mathlib's `Metric.IsSeparated ε` for some ε > 0 (strict, edist-valued), which was considered but judged less readable.
Slot (ii) is stated for general d ≥ 2 (Boshernitzan / Adiceam's form); Conway's original planar question is the case d = 2 of the same parametrized statement.

Definitions are kept inside the problem file in `namespace DanzerSet` (as e.g. Kakeya.lean does) because the task confines output to one file; `IsUniformlyDiscrete` is generic enough that a reviewer may prefer moving it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
Three trivially provable `category test` lemmas were added as basic API for the bespoke definitions (univ is Danzer; finite sets have bounded density; ∅ is uniformly discrete).

reviewer_notes: The list entry is terse; all candidates and the final file follow the Danzer-set article and Adiceam's survey: Danzer set = meets every convex body of volume 1 in ℝ^d, d ≥ 2 (d = 1 trivial via ℤ). Choices that are equivalent for the existence questions by scaling/homothety (and so not defects): ConvexBody (compact) vs arbitrary convex set of volume 1; volume exactly 1 vs any fixed positive volume; O(r^d) growth vs limsup normalized by r^d or by ball volume; strict vs non-strict separation. Boundary cases checked: `Set.ncard` infinite → 0 is guarded by an explicit Finite conjunct (tested by `not_hasBoundedDensity_univ`); volume normalization tested by `not_isDanzerSet_empty` (unit cube has volume 1). Quantifier over d: the answer is a predicate on d evaluated at the parameter d, so the theorem does not force one uniform yes/no across dimensions; the `answer(sorry) ↔` style linter does not fire on this form and repo precedent exists. No candidate omitted a slot; no decomposition objections were raised. Final file compiles with only the two `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
